newsitem.title: UK: UK to ease casino licensing from next October.
newsitem.headline: UK to ease casino licensing from next October.

text.p: Britain said on Tuesday it planned to change the way it collects duties on gaming from next October in a move to reduce the burdens for "honest traders" and make it easier for the government to crack down on illegal gaming.

Chancellor Kenneth Clarke said in his 1996 Budget that from October 1, 1997, six-month licences would no longer be issued but replaced by a registration system, similar to that for Value Added Tax (VAT), replacing the need for regular renewals.
"Once registered, casinos will only need to advise Customs and Excise of changes," the government's Customs and Excise department said in a statement.

Casinos will be able to adopt more flexible accounting periods, will no longer be required to produce a financial statement each year and groups of casinos will be able to make a single composite return, the Customes and Excise department said in a statement.
Casino's liability to duty will also no longer be dependent on their having a licence under the Gaming Act of 1968. This will make it possible to tax illegal gaming.
The revenue effect of the changes, which the department said had come after extensive consultation, is expected to be negligible, the department said.
Under previous rules, the department could only collect duty on licensed gaming. It will now have the power to impose penalties and collect duty previously evaded.
There are 117 licensed casinos in the UK.
